actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.name: seed

device.name: Berkeley Humanoid rough-terrain velocity task (Isaac Lab)

facts.text: The repository shows the training code for Berkeley Humanoid with IsaacLab
The installation guide asks for Isaac Lab v1.0.0 with Isaac Sim 4.0.0
The extension is installed from exts/berkeley_humanoid with python -m pip install -e . after Isaac Lab is installed
The documented training command runs scripts/rsl_rl/train.py with --task Velocity-Rough-Berkeley-Humanoid-v0; the play command uses Velocity-Rough-Berkeley-Humanoid-Play-v0
Velocity-Rough-Berkeley-Humanoid-v0 is registered with entry point omni.isaac.lab.envs:ManagerBasedRLEnv and env_cfg_entry_point rough_env_cfg.BerkeleyHumanoidRoughEnvCfg
Velocity-Flat-Berkeley-Humanoid-v0 is registered with the same ManagerBasedRLEnv entry point and flat_env_cfg.BerkeleyHumanoidFlatEnvCfg as its environment configuration
Velocity-Rough-Berkeley-Humanoid-Play-v0 registers rough_env_cfg.BerkeleyHumanoidRoughEnvCfg_PLAY
BerkeleyHumanoidRoughEnvCfg subclasses LocomotionVelocityRoughEnvCfg and installs BERKELEY_HUMANOID_CFG as the scene robot
The rough configuration removes the height_scan observation term and the height scanner
BerkeleyHumanoidFlatEnvCfg subclasses BerkeleyHumanoidRoughEnvCfg and changes the terrain to a plane without a terrain generator
LocomotionVelocityRoughEnvCfg subclasses ManagerBasedRLEnvCfg and defines the scene, observations, actions, commands, rewards, terminations, randomization and curriculum
The action is a joint-position target over every joint with scale 0.5 and use_default_offset=True
The policy observation group concatenates base_lin_vel, base_ang_vel, projected_gravity, velocity_commands, hip_pos, kfe_pos, ffe_pos, faa_pos, joint_vel and actions
The policy group sets enable_corruption=True and concatenate_terms=True

The hip-position term selects joints matching .*HR, .*HAA and .*HFE; the knee term .*KFE, the foot-roll term .*FFE, the foot-yaw term .*FAA, and the joint-velocity and last-action terms cover the whole joint set
The asset init_state declares 12 joints: LL_HR, LR_HR, LL_HAA, LR_HAA, LL_HFE, LR_HFE, LL_KFE, LR_KFE, LL_FFE, LR_FFE, LL_FAA and LR_FAA
The environment sets decimation 4, episode_length_s 20.0 and sim.dt 0.005 s, so one control step is 4 * 0.005 = 0.02 s
The command ranges are lin_vel_x and lin_vel_y from -1.0 to 1.0, ang_vel_z from -1.0 to 1.0 and heading from -pi to pi, resampled every 10.0 s
The reset events sample the base pose x and y from -0.5 to 0.5 and yaw from -3.14 to 3.14, the base velocities from -0.5 to 0.5 and the joint-position scale from 0.5 to 1.5
The termination terms are a time-out and an illegal contact of the torso with threshold 1.0
The training script launches the Isaac Sim application with AppLauncher
The training script imports berkeley_humanoid.tasks so the gym.register calls run
The training script creates the environment with gym.make(task, cfg=env_cfg, render_mode=...)
The training script calls env.seed(agent_cfg.seed)
setup.py declares python_requires >=3.10 and an Isaac Sim 4.0.0 classifier
The LICENCE file states SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause

determinism.notes: reset(seed=...) and cap.world.seed.v1 set the seed of the next reset.  The fake reseeds Python's random.Random and draws its three placeholder base values from it, so one seed repeats the fake's own reset and trajectory.  The upstream reset uses Isaac Lab generators (velocity_env_cfg.py:223-246) and its seeding was not observed, so the same seed is not claimed to reproduce an Isaac Sim trajectory.

gaps: the fake is a kinematic interface stand-in (F0): no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuators, sensors, terrain, noise, reward or rendering; the upstream task runs Isaac Sim 4.0.0 and Isaac Lab 1.0.0 (README.md:25-27), which this package does not install or run, and no simulator run is claimed

the fake serves one environment with a 12-value action and a 15-value observation (3 placeholder base values and the 12-value last-action term), while the upstream scene defaults to 4096 environments (velocity_env_cfg.py:347) and the policy observation group concatenates ten terms (velocity_env_cfg.py:126-143); the real flattened width is built by Isaac Lab outside the clone and was not observed, so the fake returns a smaller observation and the other terms are not covered

every observation value except the 12-value last-action tail is a fixed placeholder; no base velocity, projected gravity, command, joint position or joint velocity is simulated, and the reset randomizations of velocity_env_cfg.py:223-246 are not modelled
the fake never terminates or truncates; the configured time-out and torso-contact termination (velocity_env_cfg.py:315-318) and the time-limit rule of the external ManagerBasedRLEnv are not modelled

the upstream action space is created by the external ManagerBasedRLEnv and was not inspected; the fake exposes an unbounded 12-value Box and does not clamp, while the configured joint-position action scales by 0.5 around the default offsets (velocity_env_cfg.py:115)

the sim backend through gymnasium.make was not run: the registered task needs Isaac Lab with Isaac Sim, and the training script launches Isaac Sim and passes cfg=env_cfg to gym.make (scripts/rsl_rl/train.py:39-40 and :88-89)
no snapshot or restore: the clone shows no get_state/set_state for the environment, and the fake offers none
no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against the Berkeley Humanoid hardware

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the last world state stays readable
